original_question: Let H_k be the 2^k x 2^k Hadamard matrix from Sylvester's construction. For odd k, is the discrepancy equal to sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k), i.e., disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k)?
target_in_paper: Entry 6 (“Did just a couple of deviations suffice all along?”), Hadamard matrices subsection, Conjecture 13. The draft is capturing that conjecture almost verbatim, though the Updates section later notes that Conjecture 13 is false.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the exact subproblem in the paper: the Sylvester Hadamard family H_k, the odd-k case, and the claimed value disc(H_k) = √2·√(2^k). This is precisely the statement of Conjecture 13 in Entry 6.
missing_details: The paper defines discrepancy explicitly as disc(A) := inf_{x ∈ {±1}^n} ||Ax||_∞; your draft assumes this definition but does not state it.

The Sylvester construction is given recursively in the paper: H_0 = (1) and H_k = H_1 ⊗ H_{k-1} = [[H_{k-1}, H_{k-1}], [H_{k-1}, -H_{k-1}]]. Saying only “from Sylvester’s construction” is slightly underspecified for a stand-alone question.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether the equality holds for every odd positive integer k.
The ambient setting is over the reals: H_k is a real ±1 matrix, x ranges over {±1}^{2^k}, and ||·||_∞ is the usual ℓ_∞ norm on R^{2^k}.

The nearby paper context matters: the preceding argument constructs a specific sign vector x^♮_(k) giving the upper bound ||H_k x^♮_(k)||_∞ = √2·√(2^k) for odd k and √(2^k) for even k, so the intended question is whether that odd-k upper bound is actually optimal.
The paper positions this as a narrow Hadamard-matrix route toward Conjecture 12, namely proving that limsup_{n→∞} sup_{A ∈ {±1}^{n×n}} disc(A)/√n > 1; that motivation is implicit in your draft.

A paper-faithful caveat is missing: in the Updates section, the manuscript reports that Conjecture 13 is false, so the statement is recorded as the paper’s original conjecture rather than as a currently open problem within the compiled manuscript.
refined_question: For each k ≥ 0, let H_0 = (1) and define the Sylvester Hadamard matrices recursively by H_k = [[H_{k-1}, H_{k-1}], [H_{k-1}, -H_{k-1}]], so that H_k is a 2^k × 2^k real ±1 matrix. For an n × n real matrix A, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := inf_{x ∈ {±1}^n} ||Ax||_∞. Is it true that for every odd positive integer k, disc(H_k) = √2·√(2^k) = 2^{(k+1)/2}?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to the draft: it is exactly Conjecture 13 in the Hadamard-matrices part of Entry 6. The preceding text in Entry 6 supplies the definition of disc(A), the Sylvester recursion for H_k, and the explicit recursive sign vector x^♮_(k) that yields the candidate upper bound √2·√(2^k) when k is odd and shows why the odd case is singled out. Conjecture 12 gives the broader motivation, but your draft is not targeting that broader limsup statement; it is targeting the narrower Sylvester-Hadamard conjecture. A complete paper-faithful refinement should therefore state the discrepancy definition, the recursive construction of H_k, the quantifier “for every odd positive integer k,” and the real ℓ_∞ setting. One should also note, for accuracy about the paper as compiled, that the Updates section reports that Conjecture 13 is false.
